title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. K is a CM field of degree 2d' with maximal totally real subfield K_r. T_K = Res_{K/Q} G_m. V_{K_r} is the norm-one torus of K_r. The previous page shows that Psi_Sigma kills V_{K_r}. S_K^0 is the quotient of T_K through which Psi_Sigma factors, plausibly T_K / V_{K_r}. That is the connected Serre group S^K of K: the quotient of T_K by the Zariski closure of the units, which is V_{K_r}. E is a field receiving the embeddings. A CM structure Sigma on K with values in E is a set of d' embeddings sigma_i: K -> Ebar with {sigma_i, c sigma_i} = Hom(K, Ebar). Psi_Sigma(x) = prod sigma_i(x) is the type-norm (reflex-norm-like) map, so T_K -> S_K^0 -> T_E.

(a) Let i_K: G_m -> S_K^0 be the 'weight' homomorphism, normalised so that i_K^{d'} equals the image of the canonical inclusion i_{K/Q}: G_m -> T_K. Grothendieck claims Psi_Sigma ∘ i_K = i_{E/Q}. Proof: for x in Q^*, Psi_Sigma(i_{K/Q}(x)) = prod sigma_i(x) = x^{d'}. So the two cocharacters agree after raising to the d'-th power. Since Hom(G_m, T) is a torsion-free lattice, they are equal.

(b) The image of Psi_Sigma is Psi_Sigma(V'_K) · i_{E/Q}(G_m). Here V'_K is the maximal compact (R-anisotropic) subtorus of S_K^0, and S_K^0 = V'_K · i_K(G_m). Grothendieck leaves this as a sketch.

Question. For fixed K, do the Psi_Sigma over all CM types form a faithful family on S_K^0? Answer: yes. Let Sigma_i be Sigma with sigma_i replaced by c sigma_i.
- Then Psi_Sigma / Psi_{Sigma_i} = sigma_i / (c sigma_i).
- If x is in the kernel of Psi_Sigma and of all Psi_{Sigma_i}, then sigma_i(x) = c sigma_i(x) for every i, so x lies in K_r.
- On K_r, Psi_Sigma = N_{K_r/Q}, so x lies in V_{K_r}. Hence x is trivial in S_K^0.
- Running the argument on points over any Q-algebra Lambda gives Ker Psi_Sigma ∩ ⋂_i Ker Psi_{Sigma_i} = 1 as tori; the next page notes that K_r is stable under base change.

In lattice language: the functions Sigma and Sigma - Sigma_i = e_i - ebar_i generate {f in Z^{Hom(K,Qbar)} : f + f∘c is constant}, which is X^*(S^K). Thus the CM-type characters generate the character group, and S^K embeds into the product of the T_E. The next page asks the analogous question for E quadratic, where the answer fails for multiquadratic K.
errors: The text has 'x = V'_{K_r}'; it should read x ∈ V_{K_r} (the norm-one torus of K_r), or its image in S_K^0.

The argument as written uses only x in K^* (rational points). To conclude for tori one must use points over arbitrary Q-algebras, or argue on character lattices. Grothendieck notes this himself at the bottom of the page and on the next page.

The relation obtained after taking d'-th powers is miswritten (in the transcription and probably the manuscript) as 'i_K Psi_Sigma(x) = x^{d'}'. It should be Psi_Sigma(i_{K/Q}(x)) = x^{d'}. Passing from the d'-th power back to (a) needs the torsion-freeness of Hom(G_m, T_E), which is left implicit.
'si ceci est vrai pour tout x' should be 'for all i'. The conclusion x ∈ K_r needs the equalities sigma_i(x) = c sigma_i(x) for every i = 1..d'.
The claim S_K^0 = V'_K · i_K(G_m), used in (b), is asserted without proof.

ideas.what: S_K^0 as the quotient of Res_{K/Q} G_m by the norm-one torus of the totally real subfield, through which all CM-type norms factor
ideas.modern_name: Serre group S^K (connected Serre group of a CM field)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Abelian l-adic representations, 1968); later Langlands, Deligne, Milne-Shih

ideas.what: The type-norm map Psi_Sigma: S_K^0 -> T_E, x -> prod sigma_i(x), composed with the weight cocharacter, gives the canonical G_m -> T_E
ideas.modern_name: Reflex norm / weight cocharacter compatibility (Mumford-Tate group of CM abelian varieties contains the scalars)

ideas.what: The family of type-norm maps over all CM types of K is faithful on S_K^0, i.e. CM-type characters generate X^*(S^K)
ideas.modern_name: Serre group is generated by (embeds into the product of) Mumford-Tate tori of CM types; X^*(S^K) = {f : f + f∘c constant}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre 1968; Deligne (Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, 1982); Milne

ideas.what: The maximal R-anisotropic subtorus V'_K and the decomposition S_K^0 = V'_K · weight G_m, used to compute images
ideas.modern_name: Serre's condition / the Serre group's maximal compact torus (Deligne torus structure)

missed.claim: Historical: in the motivic Galois theory notes, Grothendieck works explicitly with the Serre torus S_K^0 of a CM field. He proves that the CM-type norms factor through it, are compatible with the weight cocharacter, and jointly embed it. This is an independent and possibly early (if indeed 1965) treatment of the Serre group as the motivic Galois group of CM motives. It is not documented in the standard histories, which credit Serre (1967-68) and later Deligne/Milne.
missed.quote: les hom psi_Sigma : S_K^0 -> T_E associés aux diverses structures CM sur K ... une famille fidèle ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on the history of the Serre group and Taniyama group as motivic Galois groups of CM motives, and on what Grothendieck knew in 1965. The mathematics itself is now standard.

missed.claim: Point (b), determining the image of Psi_Sigma through the image of the maximal compact subtorus, is left open.
missed.quote: Quelle est l'image de psi_Sigma ? ... On va bien voir au cas E = E_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the computation of Mumford-Tate groups of CM abelian varieties via reflex norms. It is well developed today, so it is not really open.

deep.surprise_reason: The results are standard: the Serre group is generated by CM types. They are proved here correctly in a few lines. The interest is historical: Grothendieck handles the Serre torus and its faithful family of reflex-type norms in the context of motivic Galois theory, possibly before or independently of Serre's published treatment. The dating is uncertain (1965 to about 1977).
transcription_corrections: 'Regardons-nous de l'homomorphisme' is probably 'Regardons maintenant l'homomorphisme'.
'i_K : G_{m,Q} -> S_K^0' is correct, but the next displayed relation is likely 'i_K(x)^{d'} = i_{K/Q}(x)', with the * being a stray mark.
'i_K psi_Sigma(x) = x^{d'}' should read psi_Sigma i_{K/Q}(x) = x^{d'}.
'(en élevant à puissance d'ièmes)' is probably '(en élevant à la puissance d'-ième)'.
'si ceci est vrai pour tout x' is likely 'si ceci est vrai pour tout i'.
'on aura en quotient' is likely 'on aura en quotientant'.
'Psi_Sigma(x)=1 revient à l'image de x dans S_K^0 -> 1' is likely 'donc l'image de x dans S_K^0 est 1'.
Last line: 'Cet argument marche aussi en remplaçant Q par une alg. quelconque Lambda', i.e. Lambda, not Q.
